summary: The anisotropic separable cube statement is proved without errors or gaps. The smallest dimensions, origin-only support, zero-energy coordinates, and zero-volume boundary fibers cause no exception. The body and actual-volume probability normalization are valid. Coordinate halving applies separately to each convex nondecreasing penalty and yields the stated second moment under the original volume law; Cauchy-Schwarz and the two Markov bounds give good-fiber mass at least one half when d >= 16 n^2. The accepted cube-cap calculation applies to the explicitly mapped normalized displacement to the origin and retains its actual squared norm in the exponent. Sign symmetry transfers its marginal cap bound to every ambient containing closed halfspace at that single fixed point. The accepted continuous centerpoint argument uses only compact support and absolute continuity, which the anisotropic marginal satisfies, and its point lies in the actual origin fiber. The complementary dimension comparison and all stated constants are correct. No exchangeability or covariance assertion from the equal-penalty predecessors is used for unequal penalties.
